subject: Plots rendering in R rather than browser

messages.author: 0bc357a2b8347256
messages.subject: Plots rendering in R rather than browser
parts:
Ok, this is a strange problem.  I've got a reactive function that generates a histogram object:

histoGraph = reactive({
       
        clust = input$clusterNum
        Dvar = input$drillDownVar
        #clust = 3
        #Dvar = "PageViews"
       
        rxSum = rxSummary(formula=as.formula(paste("~",Dvar,sep="")), data=users)
        rxMax = rxSum$sDataFrame$Max
        rxMin = rxSum$sDataFrame$Min
        rxSdv = rxSum$sDataFrame$StdDev
        rxMen = rxSum$sDataFrame$Mean
        quant = rxQuantile(varName=Dvar, users)
        xbot = rxMin
        xtop = (quant[4] - quant[2])*3 + quant[4]
       
        if(rxSdv-rxMin > 20){
            breaks = 20
        }else{
            breaks = rxSdv - rxMin
        }
       
        rxHistogram(as.formula(paste("~",Dvar)), users, histType="Percent", transformObjects=list(clust=clust, Dvar=Dvar),
            startVal=rxMin, endVal=rxSdv, numBreaks=breaks, rowSelection=(ClusterNumber==clust), xAxisMinMax=c(0,rxSdv))
})

I then want to use that object in two output functions, one to plot the histogram, and one to display the table the histogram plot is based from:

#Histogram Plot
    output$histoPlot = renderPlot({
        outputOptions(output, "histoPlot", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)
        histoGraph()
    })
   
#Histogram Table
    output$histoTable = renderTable({
        outputOptions(output, "histoTable", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)
        histObj = histoGraph()
        t(data.frame(thing = histObj$panel.args[[1]]$x, "Percent" = histObj$panel.args[[1]]$y))
    })


I find that every time I change the input, it will sometimes display the resulting plot in the browser, but sometimes it'll open up an R plot of the graph instead.  Do I need to have it do something special?  Sometimes it takes a little while to compute the histogram, would that be causing a problem?  It's especially curious that it works only every other time.

Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Plots rendering in R rather than browser
parts:
After the input changes, the next time histoGraph() is called, the histoGraph code is actually executed. After that, but before the next input change, each call to histoGraph() just returns the previous value (i.e. the value is cached until invalidation).

The problem is that the plot will only show up in the browser if histoGraph actually executes while inside renderPlot. If renderTable happens to run first, then histoGraph is going to execute outside of a renderPlot. This matters because renderPlot sets up a png() R graphics device when it starts executing its code block, and closes it when it's done.

I can't tell from looking at your code, though, what line is actually causing the histogram to be drawn; is it rxHistogram? It does a plot but also returns some data? You would need to separate those out into two separate pieces of functionality, where the latter is in the reactive({}) and the former is directly in renderPlot.

Another minor note, the calls to outputOptions only need to execute once each, so they should be moved to after the definition of their respective outputs, not nested inside of the definition.

Well, I guess you could do something like this:

# Not shown, but, change histoGraph from a reactive expression to a regular function.
# Since you're relying on its side effects, it's inherently not a good fit for reactive expression

values <- reactiveValues()
output$histoPlot <- renderPlot({
  histObj <- histoGraph()
  values$histObj <- histObj
})
outputOptions(output, "histoPlot", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)

output$histoTable = renderTable({
  histObj <- values$histObj
  if (is.null(histObj))
    NULL
  else
